title: Chicken Run
tagline: No chickens were harmed in the making of this menu.
about: A coop of chickens plan a great escape from a farm before they end up in pies.
cue: Serve the pies when Mr Tweedy runs the pie machine test.
faces: Serve the pies when Mr Tweedy runs the pie machine test.

Tweedy's Egg FarmChicken RunNo chickens were harmed in the making of this menu.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersEgg quota curried egg and cress sandwichesMild curried egg mayo with cress on soft white breadHow to make it6 eggs4 tbsp whole egg mayonnaise1/2 tsp mild curry powder1 bunch chivessalt and white pepper, to taste8 slices of soft white bread40g butter1 punnet cressBoil the eggs hard, cool in iced water and peel.Mash with the mayonnaise, curry powder, chopped chives, salt and white pepper.Butter the bread and spread the egg over half of it. Scatter with cress and close up.Cut off the crusts and cut each into 4 triangles.Babs's knitted cheese strawsTwisted puff pastry with parmesan and paprika, baked crispHow to make it2 sheets of puff pastry1 egg80g parmesan1 pinch sweet paprikaBrush one pastry sheet with beaten egg and cover with the parmesan and paprika.Lay the other sheet on top, press, cut into strips and twist.Bake at 200°C until golden and crisp.MainsPie machine beef and onion piesSlow braised beef and onion in Worcestershire gravy, baked in shortcrustHow to make it1kg beef chuck2 brown onions1 bunch thyme2 tbsp tomato paste1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce500ml beef stock2 tbsp cornflour2 sheets of shortcrust pastry2 sheets of puff pastry1 egg300g frozen peas30g butterDice the beef and slice the onions.Brown the beef in batches, add the onions, thyme, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce and stock, cover and braise.Thicken with cornflour mixed in water, then cool.Line four pie tins with shortcrust, fill, top with puff and egg wash.Bake at 200°C.Simmer the peas with the butter and mash roughly.Leek, mushroom and cheddar farm pieChickens go in, pies come out. Not this one.How to make itAs written, serves 4Leek, mushroom and potato in a creamy sharp cheddar and mustard sauce, baked under golden puff pastry with buttered peas alongside.Boil 500g diced potato for 8 minutes and drain.Soften 2 sliced leeks and 300g sliced mushrooms in 40g butter.Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 400ml milk and cook until thick.Add 150g grated cheddar, 1 tbsp wholegrain mustard and the potato.Tip into a pie dish, top with a sheet of puff pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes.Serve with 300g buttered peas.SweetsEscape plane jam roly-polyBaked roll of soft dough and raspberry jam, served with custardHow to make it100g butter250g self-raising flour150ml cold water150g raspberry jam600ml custardRub the butter into the flour, then add the water to a soft dough.Roll to a rectangle, spread with jam and roll up. Wrap loosely in baking paper and foil.Bake at 180°C.Heat the custard and serve with slices.DrinksCoop meeting honey malt hot chocolateHot milk with cocoa, malt powder and honey, topped with cream and dark chocolateHow to make it1 L full cream milk3 tbsp cocoa powder4 tbsp malted milk powder2 tbsp honey300ml thickened cream50g dark chocolateWarm the milk until steaming but not boiling. Whip the cream.Whisk in the cocoa, malt and honey until smooth and frothy.Pour into four mugs, top with cream and grate dark chocolate over.
